artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ denote the Legendre/Jacobi symbol, and for nonnegative integers write $\binom{3k}{k,k,k}=\frac{(3k)!}{(k!)^3}$.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every prime $p>5$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}}{(-960)^{3k}}\equiv\begin{cases}\left(\frac{p}{15}\right)\,(x^{2}-2p)\pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if }\left(\frac{p}{43}\right)=1\text{ and }4p=x^{2}+43y^{2}\text{ with }x,y\in\mathbb{Z},\\ 0\pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if }\left(\frac{p}{43}\right)=-1.\end{cases}$$

(b) For each integer $n\ge 2$, define
$$a_n:=\frac{1}{2n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(5418k+263)\,(-9603)^{\,n-1-k}\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}.$$
Prove or disprove that $a_n\in\mathbb{Z}$ whenever $2n+1$ is not a power of $3$, and that $3a_n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus 3\mathbb{Z}$ whenever $2n+1$ is a power of $3$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published proof or refutation of this specific conjecture (involving the summand $\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}/(-960)^{3k}$, the discriminant 43, and the integrality statement with weight $5418k+263$). Several of Z.-W. Sun's supercongruence conjectures of similar shape have been proved, but no source found directly addresses this one, so its status remains unverified.
